Subject: Redwood deployment options & migration plan

Hi Samir — thanks again for the discovery call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same page.

Key needs you mentioned:
- Low-latency inference for customer-facing chat (p50 target: ~200ms, burst to 50tps)
- Data governance: some PII stays in-house, other traffic OK to send to a managed service
- Existing stack: primary usage today via OpenAI API for prototyping; a subset of inference runs on a legacy on-prem GPU cluster for internal models
- Timeline: pilot in 4–6 weeks, rollout to production after successful pilot

What we recommend (high level):
- POC: Redwood Hosted API to get model parity quickly and validate prompts & latency with minimal integration work
- Production options: Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput and cost if you want reserved GPUs; Private VPC if legal/regulatory constraints require customer-managed networking or on-prem data residency

Open questions for you:
1) What percent of inference traffic needs to stay on-prem for compliance?
2) Any hard requirements around model pinning or quantization (we can support several quantized variants)?
3) Will you want a hybrid setup (some traffic to Hosted, some to Dedicated/private)?

Attaching a short one-pager that maps Deployment Mode -> When to use -> Requirements. I also attached an initial SOW draft for the pilot.

Next steps I propose:
- Rishi: technical readout on migration complexity (by EOD tomorrow)
- Samir/Lisa: confirm constraints (Q1 above) and available infra contacts
- Marissa/Vivek: schedule pilot kickoff for the week of 3/29 if you’re good with the approach

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks Marissa — useful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- Compliance: ~20% of traffic (customer PII) needs to remain within our VPC/on-prem for now. The rest can go to a managed API.
- Current infra: we prototype via OpenAI API. We also have a small legacy GPU cluster running some internal models (NVIDIA V100s, custom Triton stack).

We like the idea of a hybrid approach: Hosted for rapid POC + Dedicated or Private for the PII workloads.

Samir — quick technical notes after reviewing your stack notes and the hardware details you shared in the call: 

- Model compatibility: Redwood supports standard Hugging Face/transformers formats and can run TF/PyTorch-converted models. If your Triton pipeline exports models as ONNX or TorchScript, we can ingest those. Small conversion steps may be required for custom ops.
- KV cache & session continuity: For real-time chat we support hot-cache strategies. If you have an existing session storage, we can integrate KV sync or offer a proxy to preserve continuity during the hybrid handoff.
- Latency: For the p50 200ms target, Dedicated in-region (reserved) GPUs with optimized kernels is the safest path. Hosted can meet it for smaller scale during POC but may see variability at burst.
- Data residency: Private VPC (or on-prem) is the only route if the 20% PII traffic must never leave your network perimeter. We can run our private control plane + customer-managed compute in your VPC.
- Migration effort & timeline: Recommended plan:
  - Week 0–1: baseline profiling (OpenAI vs on-prem) + data flow mapping
  - Week 2–3: POC on Hosted API with representative prompts
  - Week 4–6: Dedicated/private pilot for PII traffic; sync KV sessions; finalize SSO/KMS integration

Blockers to flag early: access to model artifacts (weights), any custom CUDA kernels, and SSO/KMS certificates for private deployment. If you can share model export + a small sample workload, we’ll size the Dedicated pool and produce a pilot cost estimate.

Happy to jump on a short tech session with Lisa and your infra folks — Vivek and I can make time Wednesday or Thursday next week.

— Rishi
